questions.title: Valid Anagram
questions.statementMd:
Given two strings `s` and `t`, return `true` if `t` is an anagram of `s`, and `false` otherwise.

An anagram uses exactly the same letters the same number of times, in any order.

**Constraints**

- `1 <= s.length, t.length <= 100000`
- `s` and `t` consist of lowercase English letters.

python.driver:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys, json
    _args = [json.loads(_l) for _l in sys.stdin.read().split("\n") if _l.strip() != ""]
    _out = Solution().isAnagram(*_args)
    print(json.dumps(_out, separators=(",", ":")))

tests.explanation: Both use three a's and one each of n, g, r and m.
rat has a t that car does not have.

questions.title: Group Anagrams
questions.statementMd:
Given an array of strings `strs`, group the anagrams together.

You may return the groups, and the words inside each group, in any order. If the same word appears more than once in the input, keep every copy.

**Constraints**

- `1 <= strs.length <= 10000`
- `1 <= strs[i].length <= 100`
- `strs[i]` consists of lowercase English letters.

python.driver:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys, json
    _args = [json.loads(_l) for _l in sys.stdin.read().split("\n") if _l.strip() != ""]
    _out = Solution().groupAnagrams(*_args)
    if isinstance(_out, list):
        _out = sorted(sorted(_x) for _x in _out)
    print(json.dumps(_out, separators=(",", ":")))

tests.explanation: eat, tea and ate share letters; tan and nat share letters; bat is on its own.
Three words are rearrangements of abc and two of xyz.
